name: Milford
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Milford, MA 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Milford, MA: the Draper Memorial Park tree lighting with Santa, free photos with Santa on Main Street and the Welcome Santa Parade.
lede: Milford starts the season with a free tree lighting in Draper Memorial Park, where Santa arrives before the countdown, and keeps it going with free Santa photos by the fire on Main Street and a firefighters' parade to welcome Santa to town.
celebrates: Christmas in Milford centers on downtown Main Street. Citizens for Milford, a volunteer group, runs the Milford Christmas Tree Lighting in Draper Memorial Park, with free hot chocolate, cookies, brownies and soup, a carol sing-along led by the Greater Milford Community Chorus and a visit from Santa before the tree is lit. Milford Firefighters Local 2140 presents the Welcome Santa Christmas Parade, with floats, walkers and decorated fire trucks from businesses and groups across town. Rail Trail Flatbread Company on Main Street sets Santa by its fire for free photos on evenings through December, and the Claflin Hill Symphony Orchestra plays its Holiday Pops in the Grand Ballroom at Milford Town Hall.
lastyear: In 2025 Citizens for Milford held the tenth annual Milford Christmas Tree Lighting in Draper Memorial Park on Friday, December 5, with treats from 5:30 pm, Santa at 5:45 pm and the tree lit at 6:30 pm. Two days later, on Sunday, December 7, Milford Firefighters Local 2140 presented the Welcome Santa Christmas Parade at 4:30 pm, starting on Veterans Memorial Drive, with awards for the best decorated floats and trucks. Milford Police closed Main Street along the route from 4 pm.
facts: Milford was first settled in 1662 as part of Mendon and became its own town in 1780. The name is said to come from the fords on the Mill River that early settlers used. The town is known for Milford pink granite, which went into Memorial Hall in Milford, Worcester City Hall and the McKim Building of the Boston Public Library. Draper Memorial Park, home of the town tree, is a triangle of land downtown where Congress Street meets Main Street.
trains: Milford has no commuter rail station of its own. The closest MBTA stop is Forge Park/495, the last station on the Franklin/Foxboro Line, in neighboring Franklin, and the Franklin/Dean College station is one stop farther in. For a train ride with Christmas lights, Edaville in Carver runs its holiday train through the season, and the Old Colony and Fall River Railroad Museum in Fall River is a drive to the southeast. The Boston Street Railway Association keeps Boston-area trolley history alive.

kidfact: Milford's name comes from the mill river fords, the shallow spots where people could walk across the Mill River long before there were bridges. Some of Milford's pink granite was used to build the big Boston Public Library in Copley Square.
faq: When is the Milford tree lighting?

Citizens for Milford holds the Milford Christmas Tree Lighting in Draper Memorial Park on a Friday evening in early December. Families arrive from 5:30 pm for free hot chocolate, cookies, brownies and soup, Santa comes at 5:45 pm, carols start at 6 pm and the tree is lit at 6:30 pm. The event wraps up before 7 pm.
Is there a Christmas parade in Milford?

Yes. Milford Firefighters Local 2140 presents the Welcome Santa Christmas Parade in early December. In 2025 it stepped off at 4:30 pm on a Sunday from Veterans Memorial Drive, with floats and walkers from local businesses and groups, decorated fire trucks and awards for the best floats and trucks. Main Street closes along the route beforehand.
Where can kids get a free photo with Santa in Milford?

Rail Trail Flatbread Company at 223 Main Street hosts Photos With Santa by its fireplace on several December evenings from 5:30 to 7:30 pm and on Christmas Eve at midday. The restaurant says the photo is free, with no lines and no charge, and families can book a table if they want to eat.
Is the Milford tree lighting free?

Yes. Citizens for Milford calls the tree lighting a free community event, and the hot chocolate and snacks are free as well. The group works with the Greater Milford Community Chorus, Rail Trail Flatbread Company, the school food service, the Parks Department and the Fire Department, and the Milford Cultural Council has given grants in past years.
Can we take the train to Milford?

Milford has no commuter rail station. The nearest MBTA stop is Forge Park/495, the last station on the Franklin/Foxboro Line in neighboring Franklin, with Franklin/Dean College one stop closer to Boston. From either station families finish the trip to downtown Milford by car or rideshare.
